one_liner: Hand-written NEON straight-alpha BGRA overlay for Raspberry Pi; 3.5x its own scalar fallback on cache-resident images, 1.4-1.6x when memory-bound.
what_it_does: Blends a BGRA foreground with straight (non-premultiplied) alpha onto a BGRA background: out.RGB = (bg*(255-fg.A) + fg*fg.A)/255, out.A = bg.A. The C++ API is two templates, overlay_alpha_fast<RescaleType>(bg, fg, out, n) for equal-size images with n a multiple of 8, and overlay_alpha_stride<RescaleType>(bg, fg, out, bg_full_cols, fg_rows, fg_cols, fg_full_cols) for a smaller foreground placed in a larger background. Five extern "C" wrappers (overlay_alpha_stride_div255_round and so on) cover the stride variant. out may alias bg for in-place compositing.
how_it_is_fast: It processes 8 pixels per step: vld4_u8 de-interleaves B, G, R and A into four 8-lane registers, vmull_u8 widens fg*alpha and bg*(255-alpha) to 16 bits, and the result goes back through vst4_u8. The divide by 255 is a multiply-high by a reciprocal constant (0x8080 after adding 128 for exact rounding, 0x8081 for floor) with vuzp2q/vshrn narrowing. Optional cheaper modes divide by 256 with a single shift. Rows are split across cores with '#pragma omp parallel for'.
when_to_use: Compositing an RGBA/BGRA overlay (HUD, watermark, sprite) onto camera or video frames on a Raspberry Pi or other AArch64/ARMv7 board with NEON.
Small to medium overlays whose three buffers fit in L2 (up to about 200x200 px on a Pi 3B+ with 512 KB L2), where the measured gain is 3.4-3.6x.
Frame-rate pipelines that can live with a 1.4-1.6x gain once images are memory-bound (300-5000 px squares in the published runs).
Code that already uses straight alpha with an opaque background and BGRA byte order (OpenCV CV_8UC4 BGRA mats work directly).
when_not_to_use: Tiny overlays (under about 32x32 px): a fixed per-call cost of about 20 us dominates and NEON was 0.93-1.1x there in the published runs.
Backgrounds that are not opaque or need true Porter-Duff 'over' semantics: background alpha is copied, not composited (open issue #1: a transparent background gives a transparent result).
Premultiplied-alpha pipelines, other channel orders, 16-bit or float images: only 8-bit BGRA straight alpha is implemented.
Proprietary code that cannot take GPL-3.0, or projects that need a maintained library: no commits since 2020-07-26, no releases.
x86 production use: the x86-64 path only translates the NEON intrinsics to SSE4 through Intel's NEON_2_SSE header and was never benchmarked.

integration.dependencies: none at runtime beyond OpenMP (libgomp) when found; the top-level CMakeLists.txt does find_package(GTest REQUIRED), and OpenCV is optional (examples). x86 builds need Intel's ARM_NEON_2_x86_SSE header.
integration.min_toolchain: CMake 3.11; C++ standard not set (compiler default); the published binaries were built with GCC 9.2.0 (crosstool-NG cross toolchain); the scalar fallback's '#pragma GCC unroll' needs GCC 8+
integration.platforms: aarch64 NEON (A64 path with vmull_high/vuzp2), ARMv7/A32 NEON (vuzpq path), x86-64 via NEON_2_SSE with -msse4; DISABLE_NEON gives a portable scalar fallback
integration.thread_safety: Stateless functions with no globals; each call opens its own OpenMP parallel region over rows. Concurrent calls are not documented.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: the baseline is the same library built with -DDISABLE_NEON=ON, so the API is identical, but there is no drop-in for OpenCV addWeighted or other blend APIs

gotchas: Harness note (read from the committed binaries): both aarch64 .so files used for the CSVs (byte-identical at the results commit a6c7d04 and HEAD) link libgomp and call GOMP_parallel, so OpenMP was on in both builds and the thread count was not recorded; the .comment section names GCC 9.2.0 (crosstool-NG). The no-simd build's Div255_Round stride kernel has zero vector instructions (llvm-objdump: ldrb/strb/mul/madd only), so GCC 9.2 did not auto-vectorize the fallback despite its ivdep/unroll pragmas; the README's 'GCC -O3 vs NEON' is in practice NEON vs plain scalar code.

The 3.5x headline holds only while bg, fg and out fit in the Pi 3B+'s 512 KB L2: NEON goes from 2.8 ns/px at 200 px to 5.8 ns/px at 250 px and about 7.4 ns/px beyond 300 px, while scalar stays at 10-12 ns/px, so the ratio falls to 1.33-1.65x (derived from page data).

Timing is from Python ctypes with one run per size and no warm-up; the 200 px point of the small sweep is just 10 calls (about 1.3 ms total). perf_test.py uses np.int, removed in NumPy 1.24, so it fails on current NumPy without a one-line edit.

Div255_Round_Approx differs by build: the NEON version is one too large for 127 of 65536 inputs, while the scalar fallback maps it to the exact div255_round. The tail path for widths not a multiple of 8 runs the 8-pixel kernel on partly uninitialised stack buffers (only valid lanes are copied out). The library also needs GTest installed to configure, and every target builds with -Werror -pedantic-errors.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the catalogued SIMD siblings does alpha compositing: qAverageColor and bilinear_filter_simd are x86 pixel kernels for other operations, and EVE or the Vector Class Library are general SIMD toolkits on which you would write this kernel yourself. Pick this when you want a ready, readable NEON BGRA overlay for Pi-class ARM and GPL-3.0 is acceptable.
verified_claims_summary: On a Raspberry Pi 3B+ (Ubuntu 20.04 64-bit), overlay_alpha_stride_div255_round in the NEON build was compared with the same library built with DISABLE_NEON (GCC 9.2.0, -O3 per the README, OpenMP on in both, the baseline left fully scalar by the compiler), timed through Python ctypes on random square images. It ran 3.4-3.6x faster at 128-200 px squares, 0.93x at 1 px, and 1.33-1.65x from 300 to 5000 px, where both are limited by memory bandwidth (derived from page data).
status_note: Abandoned since 2020-07-26 (25 commits, no releases, one open issue unanswered since 2022). The core is a single 200-line .cpp plus two headers and easy to vendor, but GPL-3.0 limits copying into proprietary code.
